name: apply_relocation_records
description: Walks a list of relocation records, each giving a count and a run of offsets, and adds a value to the longword at every offset, with the value found by following a chain of entries in a table. It zeroes each record as it is consumed and does nothing unless the list header carries the expected marker.

name: stub_return_only
description: Routine consisting only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use, so it performs no work.

name: load_hunks_and_relocate
description: Program entry that walks an executable image, checks each block header against the loader's block type codes, allocates memory for each block through the system library and copies its contents in. It then applies the relocation records that follow each block before returning.

name: spin_down_word_counter
description: Counts a 16-bit register down through zero until it wraps around, with no other effect. It is a pure timing loop that touches no memory or hardware.

name: stub_return_only
description: Routine consisting only of a return, with no calls, memory access or hardware register use, so it performs no work.

name: decode_backward_lz_stream
description: Decodes a compressed stream into a buffer working from the end towards the start, reading run-length codes from a bit reader and either copying literal bytes or repeating bytes from a distance behind the output position. It stores the final output position in a global variable when the output reaches the start of the buffer.

name: extract_bits_from_bitstream
description: Shifts a requested number of bits out of a packed bitstream one at a time, carrying them through a 32-bit working register and refilling it from memory when the source runs empty. The collected bits form the result.

name: trap_then_invalidate_cache
description: Raises processor trap number six, then calls the cache invalidation routine. The bytes after that call decode as invalid instructions, so the routine ends there.

name: invoke_vector_twice_store_results
description: Program entry that clears a byte before each of two calls through a library function vector, storing each returned value into a global slot. It then calls three further routines and returns zero.

name: call_three_routines_return_zero
description: Calls three other routines in sequence and returns zero, adding no work of its own.

name: store_four_call_results
description: Calls four other routines in turn and stores each returned value into one of four fixed slots at offsets from a base register.

name: call_vector_and_bias_result
description: Calls a function through a pointer stored at a fixed offset from the global base. If the call returns a non-zero value it returns that value plus 32768, otherwise it returns zero.

name: free_memory_via_library
description: Calls the system memory-release routine through a function vector held at a fixed offset from the global base, then returns.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero immediately and performs no other work.

name: retry_open_library_until_ok
description: Repeatedly calls the system library-open routine through its function vector until it returns a non-zero handle, with no other work in the loop.

name: close_library_via_vector
description: Closes a system library through its function vector at a fixed offset from the global base, then returns.

name: call_single_routine_passthrough
description: Calls one other routine and returns immediately afterwards, doing nothing else.

name: copy_bytes_with_zero_terminator
description: Copies a byte sequence from a source pointer to a destination pointer, moving eight bytes at a time for the bulk and single bytes for the remainder. It then writes a zero byte after the last copied byte.

name: clear_two_globals_and_call
description: Clears two global variables to zero, calls one other routine, and returns the address of this routine.

name: repeat_call_until_zero_flag
description: Calls one other routine repeatedly and keeps looping until the zero condition flag is set, then returns.

name: allocate_sized_block_and_link
description: Allocates a block of the requested size through the memory-allocation vector and, on success, records the size in the block header and links the block into a list, returning the address just past that header. On failure it calls a cleanup routine and raises a trap.

name: free_listed_block_or_allocate
description: Searches a linked list for the block at the given address; if it is found, the block is unlinked and returned through the memory-free vector. If it is not found and a sentinel counter is zero, it allocates a new list entry through the allocation vector, links it at the head, and otherwise falls through to a trap.

name: find_list_tail
description: Follows next-pointers through a linked list until it reaches an entry whose link is zero, then stores that last entry's address in a global slot.

name: preserve_global_across_two_calls
description: Saves a global variable, calls two other routines, then writes the saved value back so those calls leave the global unchanged.

name: preserve_global_across_two_calls
description: Saves a global variable, calls two other routines, then writes the saved value back so those calls leave the global unchanged.

name: allocate_sized_block_and_link
description: Allocates a block of the requested size through the memory-allocation vector and, on success, records the size in the block header and links the block into a list, returning the address just past that header. On failure it calls a cleanup routine and raises a trap.

name: free_listed_block_or_allocate
description: Searches a linked list for the block at the given address; if it is found, the block is unlinked and returned through the memory-free vector. If it is not found and a sentinel counter is zero, it allocates a new list entry through the allocation vector, links it at the head, and otherwise falls through to a trap.

name: unlink_block_from_list
description: Walks a linked list to find the entry whose link points to the given block, then removes that link and releases the block through the memory-free vector. If the block is not in the list, it allocates a new list header through the allocation vector and links it at the head, raising a trap if allocation fails.

name: allocate_block_at_list_head
description: Allocates a block through the memory-allocation vector and links it at the head of a list, storing the previous head as its first longword and clearing the second. If allocation fails it calls a cleanup routine and raises a trap.

name: free_all_list_entries
description: Releases the first list entry through the memory-free vector, then walks the chain of entries attached to it and releases each one.

name: zero_memory_from_own_address
description: Stores a routine address in a global variable, raises trap number zero, clears that variable, then zeroes memory in longword steps from this routine's own address up to a fixed upper bound.

name: draw_text_and_setup_copper
description: Draws zero-terminated text strings into bitplane memory by copying eight glyph rows per character from a font table, with a line stride of 80 bytes per row. It then points the copper list at the buffer, waits on a flag, and writes DMA and interrupt control registers.

name: stub_return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one as its result and performs no other work.

name: open_libraries_and_init_data
description: Opens a sequence of system libraries through their function vectors, stopping early if any open returns nothing, then copies a block of data one longword at a time into a fixed buffer. It then calls several library vectors and closes the library handles before returning.
